Convert sequence input to the canonical form used by lag sequential analysis

Source: R/lsa-data.R
lsa_data.Rd

lsa_data() converts the forms in which sequence data usually arrive into the canonical representation used by lag sequential analysis, and it is what lsa() calls on its input. A lag sequential analysis needs, for every sequence, the ordered list of coded events, and a common set of state labels across sequences. Transitions are counted within sequences only, so the boundaries between sequences must be kept.

Accepted forms are:

  • an atomic vector of codes (one sequence);

  • a list of vectors (several sequences);

  • a wide matrix or data frame, one row per sequence and one column per ordered time point;

  • a square numeric matrix of transition counts, row i and column j holding the count of i -> j (any square numeric matrix is read this way, so pass square integer-coded sequences as a data frame);

  • a sequence object: a tna or group_tna model with its data, a tna_seq_data, tna_data or nestimate_data object, a Nestimate netobject, or a TraMineR stslist.

NA and empty strings are treated as missing observations, not as a state: they are dropped wherever they occur and the surrounding events close up. To model missingness as a state, recode it (for example to "missing") first. A transition-count matrix carries no sequences, so the functions that resample sequences (bootstrap_lsa(), permute_lsa(), stability_lsa(), reliability_lsa(), compare_lsa()) cannot be used on a fit built from it. Long event logs are read by lsa() through its actor and action arguments.

Usage

lsa_data(x, labels = NULL)

Arguments

x

Sequence input in one of the forms listed above. An lsa_data object is returned unchanged.

labels

Optional character vector of state names. Default NULL takes the sorted distinct values of character input, the levels of a factor, or "Code 1", "Code 2", ... for integer codes. When supplied, character codes are matched to it by name and integer codes index into it.

Value

An object of class c("lsa_data", "list"). Print it for the input source, the number of states, sequences, events and lag-1 transitions; read the events with as.data.frame() (one row per event, or per cell for a transition matrix). The object stores the integer-coded events and their sequence membership (NULL for a transition matrix), the state labels, the counts of states, sequences and events, and the source ("events" or "transitions").

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and lagdynamics_bad_input: an unsupported input type, no usable events, invalid counts in a transition matrix, invalid integer codes, or codes that do not match labels.

See also

as.data.frame.lsa_data() for the event table; lsa_transitions() for transition counts; lsa().

Examples

lsa_data(engagement)
#> <lsa_data>
#>   source:        events
#>   states (K):    3
#>   labels:        Active, Average, Disengaged
#>   sequences:     136
#>   events:        1870
#>   transitions:   1734 (lag 1, summed across sequences)

# Several sequences: no transition is counted across the boundary
lsa_data(list(c("a", "b", "a"), c("b", "c", "a", "b")))
#> <lsa_data>
#>   source:        events
#>   states (K):    3
#>   labels:        a, b, c
#>   sequences:     2
#>   events:        7
#>   transitions:   5 (lag 1, summed across sequences)

# A transition-count matrix
counts <- matrix(c(0, 3, 1, 2, 0, 4, 5, 1, 0), 3, 3,
                 dimnames = list(c("a", "b", "c"), c("a", "b", "c")))
lsa_data(counts)
#> <lsa_data>
#>   source:        transitions
#>   states (K):    3
#>   labels:        a, b, c
#>   transitions:   16 (from input matrix)
